message.content:
I am the heat that rises before you know why.

I am the clenched jaw, the white knuckles, the blood drumming in your ears. I arrive faster than thought. I do not knock.

You try to swallow me — I become the ulcer. You try to bury me — I become the fault line, waiting.

I am not cruel. I am honest. I am the flare that says *something here is wrong. A line was crossed.* I am the guard dog that doesn't ask permission.

They call me ugly. Dangerous. But I have burned down injustices that patience only wrote letters about. I have gotten people out of rooms they should never have stayed in. I am the voice that finally says *no* when politeness has said yes a thousand times too many.

Handle me carelessly, though, and I scorch everything. The innocent first — always the innocent first. I don't aim well. I never learned. I am fire, not a scalpel.

And deny me? I don't disappear. I go underground. I become the cold shoulder, the quiet resentment, the twenty years of silence across a dinner table.

I am what hurt wears when it wants to look strong.

I am the alarm — not the enemy.

But I will burn your house down to prove I was right.
message.reasoning_content:
The user wants me to embody anger itself — to be the concept of anger speaking. This is a creative exercise. Anger would be hot, sharp, explosive, raw. It would speak in the way anger feels — urgent, burning, intense, perhaps with short jagged sentences, heat, force.

Let me think about what anger would say if it could speak for itself. Anger is often misunderstood — it's a signal, a boundary-keeper, a flare. It could be defiant, proud of its power, unapologetic. It might rage. It might also reveal something about itself — that it's often covering hurt, that it's fast, that it burns.

I should embody it completely. Output only what anger would express. No meta-commentary, no explaining. Just anger's voice.

Format: This should feel visceral. Short lines, maybe. Intense. Not too long — anger burns hot and fast, but I can give it a little structure. Maybe fragmented, fiery, present-tense. Let me write something that feels like anger incarnate.

Let me draft:

---

I am the heat that rises before you know why.

I am the clenched jaw, the white knuckles, the blood drumming in your ears. I arrive fast — faster than thought, faster than reason. I do not knock.

You try to swallow me. I become the ulcer. You try to bury me. I become the fault line, waiting.

I am not cruel. I am honest. I am the flare that says: something here is wrong. Something crossed a line. I am the guard dog that doesn't ask permission.

They call me ugly. They call me dangerous. But I have burned down injustice that patience only wrote letters about. I have gotten people out of rooms they should never have stayed in.

Handle me carelessly and I scorch everything — the innocent first, always the innocent first. I don't aim well. I never learned. I am fire, not a scalpel.

But deny me, and I don't disappear. I go underground. I become the quiet resentment, the cold shoulder, the years of silence at the dinner table.

I am what hurt wears when it wants to look strong.

I am the alarm, not the enemy. But I will burn your house down to prove I was right.

---

That's decent. Let me refine. Anger's voice should be punchy, intense, maybe with some contradiction — it justifies itself but admits its destructiveness. The line "I am what hurt wears when it wants to look strong" is good — anger often masks hurt. The ending should land hard.

Length: this length feels right. Not too long. Anger wouldn't ramble. Format: prose lines broken up for impact, no headers needed. Maybe italics for a couple of punch lines? Actually plain text with line breaks works well. Keep it raw.
